name: Immunodeficiency due to selective anti-polysaccharide antibody deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for selective anti-polysaccharide antibody deficiency

criteria.description: Demonstrated impaired antibody response to polysaccharide antigens despite normal total immunoglobulin levels
History of recurrent bacterial respiratory tract infections such as sinusitis, otitis media, or pneumonia
Normal serum levels of IgG, IgA, and IgM
Exclusion of other primary or secondary immunodeficiencies by clinical and laboratory evaluation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of impaired polysaccharide antibody response with normal immunoglobulin levels and recurrent bacterial respiratory infections, after exclusion of other immunodeficiencies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires specialized immunological testing including assessment of antibody response to pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccines.

searchTerms: poor antibody response to polysaccharide antigens

pathognomonic.symptomName: Decreased specific antibody response to polysaccharide vaccine
Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to pneumococcus vaccine
searchTerms: no antibody response to pneumococcus vaccine

pathognomonic.symptomName: Decreased specific antibody response to protein-conjugated polysaccharide vaccine
searchTerms: reduced antibody response to conjugate vaccine
weak immune response to protein-linked vaccine

pathognomonic.symptomName: Complete or near-complete absence of specific antibody response to Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine
searchTerms: no antibody response to Hib vaccine
absent immunity after Haemophilus influenzae vaccine

common.symptomName: Decreased proportion of memory B cells
Recurrent bacterial upper respiratory tract infections
searchTerms: frequent bacterial sinus and throat infections
repeated bacterial infections in upper airways

common.symptomName: Recurrent upper and lower respiratory tract infections
searchTerms: frequent upper and lower respiratory infections
low B cell count in blood
decreased white blood cells that make antibodies

laboratory: Normal quantitative serum immunoglobulins (IgG, IgA, IgM)
Poor antibody response to polysaccharide vaccines (e.g., pneumococcal vaccine)
imaging: Chest radiograph or CT showing bronchiectasis in some cases
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; diagnosis based on functional antibody testing
other: Clinical history of recurrent bacterial infections

distinguishingFeatures: Low total immunoglobulin levels (especially IgG and IgA)
Broader antibody deficiency including protein antigens
Impaired antibody response to specific protein antigens rather than polysaccharides
May have normal or low immunoglobulin levels

references: Orange JS, et al. Use and interpretation of diagnostic vaccination in primary immunodeficiency: a working group report of the Basic and Clinical Immunology Interest Section of the American Academy of Allergy, Asthma & Immunology. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2012.
Bonilla FA, et al. Practice parameter for the diagnosis and management of primary immunodeficiency. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2015.
